source.title: Hyaluronic Acid: A Key Ingredient in the Therapy of Inflammation

extraction_metadata.scope_note: This is a narrative review. Review-level objectives, syntheses, figures, explicit limitations, disclosures, and author conclusions were atomized. Experimental findings from cited studies are represented only as secondary reports using atom_kind=other and tags such as secondary_reported_result; they are not represented as primary-study quantitative_result atoms.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review aims to discuss advances in treating inflammatory diseases with hyaluronic acid, focusing essentially on studies published from 2017 through 2021.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This review aims to discuss the advances that have been achieved in the treatment of inflammatory diseases using hyaluronic acid as a key ingredient, essentially focusing on studies carried out between the years 2017 and 2021.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review describes high-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid as generally antiangiogenic and immunosuppressive in intact tissues, whereas smaller fragments can signal distress and promote inflammation and angiogenesis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HMWHA, usually greater than 1000 kDa, is present in intact tissues and is antiangiogenic and immunosuppressive

atoms.canonical_statement: Hyaluronic acid is synthesized at the inner plasma membrane by HAS-1, HAS-2, and HAS-3 rather than by Golgi-associated synthesis.
The review describes hyaluronic-acid degradation through hyaluronidase-mediated cleavage and nonspecific oxidative damage from reactive oxygen species.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The degradation of HA (Figure 3) in the human body is carried out by two distinct mechanisms: one is specific, mediated by enzymes (hyaluronidases, HYALs), while the other is non-specific, determined by oxidative damage due to reactive oxygen species

atoms.canonical_statement: Reported hyaluronic-acid half-lives vary substantially by compartment, from about 24 hours in blood to about 70 days in vitreous humor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the half-life of HA in the skin is 1–2 days, the half-life in the bloodstream about 24 h, in the eye, it is 24–36 h, 1–3 weeks in the cartilage and about 70 days in vitreous humor

atoms.canonical_statement: At neutral pH, hyaluronic acid can retain water up to approximately 10,000 times its own weight.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HA attracts water molecules and can contain up to 10,000 times its weight in water

atoms.canonical_statement: The review attributes to hyaluronic acid biological roles in lubrication, hydration, extracellular-matrix structure, tissue repair, and regulation of cellular interactions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HA can be involved in several cellular interactions (differentiation, proliferation, development and recognition) and biological functions (lubrication, hydration, matrix structure and steric interactions)

atoms.canonical_statement: The review organizes hyaluronic-acid action into passive structural effects and receptor-mediated signaling effects.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HA performs its biological functions according to two basic mechanisms: (I) it can act as a passive structural molecule and (II) as a signalling molecule

atoms.canonical_statement: Hyaluronic-acid effects can differ with molecular weight, location, receptor expression, signaling pathways, and cell-cycle state, including opposing pro- and anti-inflammatory actions.
CD44 is presented as a broadly expressed hyaluronic-acid receptor whose binding and downstream effects vary with hyaluronic-acid molecular weight.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Recognized for its ability to bind to HA, cluster-determinant 44 (CD44) is widely distributed in transmembrane glycoproteins

atoms.canonical_statement: The review states that high-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid can cluster CD44 receptors and suppress pro-inflammatory mediators, whereas smaller fragments engage fewer CD44 sites and can produce different effects.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HMWHA is able to group receptors on the surface of the cell membrane to modulate receptor activity

atoms.canonical_statement: RHAMM/CD168 is described as a hyaluronic-acid receptor involved in growth-factor responses, cell migration, and tissue repair.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It is RHAMM that regulates cellular responses to growth factors and plays a role in cell migration

atoms.canonical_statement: ICAM-1 is described as a hyaluronan-binding receptor relevant to inflammatory leukocyte adhesion and migration.
Figure 1 depicts the repeating D-glucuronic-acid and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine units of hyaluronic acid and marks glycosidic and hydrogen bonding.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Figure 1. Chemical structure of hyaluronic acid (HA), where the disaccharide units that compose it are shown: D-glucuronic acid and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.

atoms.canonical_statement: Figure 2 schematically depicts hyaluronic-acid synthesis by HAS-1, HAS-2, and HAS-3 with extrusion to the extracellular space.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Figure 2. Schematic representation of the synthesis of HA by hyaluronan synthases (HAS-1, HAS-2 and HAS-3) where the placement of HA in the extracellular space is evidenced.

atoms.canonical_statement: Figure 3 schematically depicts enzymatic and reactive-oxygen-species pathways for hyaluronic-acid degradation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Figure 3. Representative scheme of enzymatic and ROS degradation of HA.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review presents intra-articular hyaluronic acid as a widely studied osteoarthritis strategy and surveys formulations designed to prolong residence, deliver active agents, reduce inflammation, and protect cartilage.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Table 1 summarizes the studies presented throughout this review for the treatment of osteoarthritis, where the beneficial role of HA is evidenced.

atoms.canonical_statement: Table 1 compiles 20 hyaluronic-acid-based osteoarthritis formulations spanning liposomes, micelles, conjugates, scaffolds, hydrogels, nanoparticles, polymers, and combination approaches.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Table 1. Study summaries, with HA, for the treatment of OA.

atoms.canonical_statement: The osteoarthritis table reports outcomes centered on pain control, reduced inflammation, cartilage protection or regeneration, and suppression of disease progression across heterogeneous in vitro and animal studies.
For rheumatoid arthritis, the review emphasizes CD44-overexpressing activated macrophages as a targeting rationale for hyaluronic-acid drug-delivery systems.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CD44 is an adhesion receptor that is often overexpressed on the surface of activated macrophages in patients with RA. Thus, due to its ability to bind to CD44, HA was selected as a target molecule for the development of new RA therapies

atoms.canonical_statement: Table 2 compiles 12 hyaluronic-acid-based rheumatoid-arthritis delivery strategies, including lipid and polymeric nanoparticles, liposomes, conjugates, hydrogels, nanomicelles, nanogels, and gold nanocages.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Table 2. Study summaries with HA, for the treatment of RA.

atoms.canonical_statement: The rheumatoid-arthritis table reports secondary outcomes including reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, improved drug retention or bioavailability, reduced inflammatory activity, and preservation of bone or cartilage.

In tendinopathy, the review describes clinical and preclinical work in which hyaluronic-acid injection is associated with pain reduction and functional or structural improvement, while noting heterogeneous methods and products.

For intervertebral-disc injury, the review discusses hyaluronic-acid-containing hydrogels and extracellular-matrix scaffolds as regenerative approaches intended to restore disc hydration, cell viability, and matrix organization.
In inflammatory skin models, the review reports that hyaluronic acid can mitigate ethanol-associated cytotoxicity and inflammatory-marker release in cultured skin cells.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The results report that the treatment of cells with ethanol increased cytotoxicity, as well as the release of pro-inflammatory

atoms.canonical_statement: During wound healing, the review describes hyaluronic acid as accumulating at the wound site and modulating inflammatory-cell and fibroblast migration, cytokine synthesis, and phagocytosis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During the inflammatory phase of healing, HA accumulates in the wound bed and acts as an inflammation regulator

atoms.canonical_statement: Table 3 summarizes five wound-healing approaches using hyaluronic acid or hyaluronic-acid-derived hydrogels, with reported secondary outcomes including shorter healing time, cytokine reduction, growth-factor expression, tissue repair, and reduced wound area.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Table 3. Study summaries where HA is used for wound-healing.

atoms.canonical_statement: For inflammatory bowel disease, the review identifies increased CD44 expression at inflamed sites as a rationale for hyaluronic-acid-mediated targeted delivery to intestinal mucosa.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Endothelial cells are known to express high levels of CD44 in inflamed IBD sites

atoms.canonical_statement: The review reports that an HA/5-ASA conjugate, IBD98-M, reduced intestinal inflammation and promoted mucosal healing in an experimental ulcerative-colitis model.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Treatment with IBD98-M has been shown to significantly reduce intestinal inflammation and promote colon-mucosa-healing

atoms.canonical_statement: Table 4 summarizes six hyaluronic-acid-based inflammatory-bowel-disease strategies, with secondary reports of mucosal healing, reduced inflammation, tissue regeneration, symptom relief, and restoration of epithelial barrier function.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Table 4. Study summaries using with HA for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.

atoms.canonical_statement: In a Calu-3 cell model, the review reports that a urea-crosslinked hyaluronic-acid/sodium-ascorbyl-phosphate construct reduced IL-6 and reactive oxygen species and improved cell healing relative to several comparator formulations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HA-CL-SAP significantly decreased IL-6 and ROS levels, and improved cell-healing

atoms.canonical_statement: The review describes hyaluronic acid as supporting oral-tissue structural integrity, osmotic regulation, and lubrication and surveys its use in gingival and periodontal inflammation.

source_anchor.paragraph: 5.8 Inflammatory Diseases of the Oral Cavity
source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In the oral cavity, HA supports the structural integrity and homeostasis of tissues that regulate osmotic pressure and tissue lubrication

atoms.canonical_statement: In a bladder-cell inflammation model, the review reports that hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulfate, and their combination reduced inflammatory signaling and moved measured markers toward a more physiological state.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the inflammation was reduced in the presence of HA, CS and the combination of both (HA/CS)

atoms.canonical_statement: For acute kidney injury, the review reports an HA-curcumin prodrug with greater solubility than free curcumin, preferential tubular-epithelial-cell uptake, and greater renal accumulation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the solubility of HA-CUR was increased compared to free CUR

atoms.canonical_statement: In a rat myocardial-infarction model, the review reports that hyaluronic-acid oligosaccharides reduced infarct size and apoptosis and promoted angiogenic and repair responses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Studies carried out on an MI model (subacute model of rat) show that o-HA can reduce the size of the infarction and the apoptosis

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that hyaluronic acid has broad therapeutic potential because of its biophysical and biological properties, extending well beyond cosmetic use.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: HA has an excellent potential for a wide range of applications, which comprise much more than the facial treatments with which it is typically associated.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors identify hyaluronic-acid interactions with receptors such as CD44 on activated macrophages as a key rationale for targeted delivery and anti-inflammatory applications.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It is the interaction with these receptors that enables the targeted delivery to target locations, resulting in greater cellular uptake and, therefore, beneficial results in reducing inflammation.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that more studies are needed to prolong hyaluronic-acid circulation and residence time and to better understand degradation mechanisms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: more studies should be carried out with the aim of obtaining prolonged circulation and a longer time in situ. A more detailed understanding of the degradation mechanisms of HA will also be essential

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors identify the relatively short half-life of hyaluronic acid in biological fluids as a major delivery limitation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The major complications associated with the delivery of HA are due to its relatively short half-life in biological fluids.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors caution that crosslinking used to extend hyaluronic-acid persistence can increase toxicity compared with free hyaluronic acid.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: it is often necessary to resort to crosslinking techniques, which can lead to greater toxicity compared to “free” HA.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors identify solution viscosity as a potential obstacle to administration or effectiveness of hyaluronic-acid formulations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The viscosity of HA solutions can also raise some questions, as this can hamper the administration or effectiveness of the developed models.

atoms.canonical_statement: Despite delivery limitations, the authors conclude that the studies reviewed show promising results for hyaluronic acid in inflammatory pathologies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the studies reviewed here show promising results for the use of HA in the treatment of inflammatory pathologies.
